description.narrative:
Impact: Afghan women and girls have their human rights protected and promoted through access to essential services, humanitarian assistance, livelihoods and income opportunities, improved voice and agency and support from a resilient Afghan women's movement.
OUTCOME 1.1 By the end of 2025, more people in Afghanistan, particularly the most marginalized, will be able to equitably access essential services that meet minimum quality standards.
OUTCOME 1.2 By the end of 2025, more people in Afghanistan, notably women and vulnerable groups, will benefit from an increasingly inclusive economy, with greater equality of economic opportunities, jobs, more resilient livelihoods, strengthened food value chains, and improved natural resources management.
OUTCOME 1.3 By the end of 2025, more people in Afghanistan can participate in an increasingly socially cohesive, gender equal, and inclusive society, where the rule of law and human rights are progressively upheld, and more people can participate in governance and decision-making.
Outcome 1.4: By end of 2025, the UN system in Afghanistan, Member States and regional organizations effectively contribute to progress on gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls in Afghanistan.

Insatsen fokuserar på att skydda och främja afghanska kvinnor och flickors mänskliga rättigheter genom tillgång till nödvändig service, humanitärt bistånd, försörjning och inkomstmöjligheter, möjligheter att delta och göra sina röster hörda samt en motståndskraftig afghansk kvinnorörelse.

The contribution is aiming to protect and promote Afghan women and girls human rights through access to essential services, humanitarian assistance, livelihoods and income opportunities, improved voice and agency and support from a resilient Afghan women's movement.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Despite severe restrictions, de facto authority (DFA) decrees, and overlapping humanitarian crises, UN Women Afghanistan maintained operations across five core thematic areas in 2025: Ending Violence Against Women, Gender in Humanitarian Action, Rebuilding the Women's Movement, Women's Economic Empowerment, and Women, Peace, and Security.
Essential Services Access: Through 83 community-based centers, temporary service points, and a helpline, UN Women directly provided multi-sectoral services and life-saving assistance to 239,873 women and girls.
Economic Opportunities: Supported 4,130 women entrepreneurs and 940 Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through business training, loans, value-chain interventions, and access to local/international trade markets.
Civil Society & Leadership: Sustained partnerships with 191 women's organizations, distributing $3.47 million in core grants to bolster organizational resilience. Provided protection and emergency assistance to 405 Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs).
System-Wide Coordination: Permanent Chairing of the Gender in Humanitarian Action Working Group (GIHA WG) helped secure $5.07 million in Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund allocations for eight women-led organizations (WLOs)triple the 2024 amount.
Results through Private Sector & Corporate Actors
Change Achieved: Fostered commitment to gender-inclusive workplaces despite nationwide restrictions on female employment. This resultet in 62 Afghan companies signed the Women's Empowerment Principles (WEPs), pledging to adopt gender-responsive workplace practices and maintain female employment.
Value chain partnerships created 4 Milk Collection Centres in the Eastern region, integrating over 400 smallholder women farmers into stable supply chains and creating 40 long-term positions. Additionally, 110 jobs were directly created or sustained within women-owned businesses.
Local communities and grassroots leaders
Change Achieved: Shifted social norms and sustained grassroots safety nets in remote, conservative areas where formal legal protections were dismantled.
Example: Trained 1,200 self-help group members to act as initial community responders for gender-based violence (GBV) cases, providing localized support and safe referrals.
Example: Engaged 12,767 men and boys in targeted psychosocial, health, and literacy programs to address harmful gender norms and prevent violence at the household level.
Media and information actors
Change Achieved: Preserved womens public presence, leadership, and educational content within a heavily censored media environment.
Example: Supported 5 gender-focused media outlets across Badakhshan, Badghis, and Kabul, sustaining 95 staff jobs (67 women). These outlets trained 138 young journalists and broadcast over 571 radio programs on women's rights framed through culturally sensitive perspectives (e.g., grounding property rights in Islamic teachings and education in the Quranic principle Iqra), reaching over 10 million listeners.
International and UN actors
Change Achieved: Embedded gender disaggregated data into system-wide humanitarian planning and response frameworks.
Example: Led the integration of sex- and age-disaggregated data into 75% of sector planning for the Afghanistan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) 2025.
Example: Collaborated with UNOCHA to establish Afghanistan's first-ever Anticipatory Action Framework jointly backed by the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) and the Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund (AHF). This resulted in a proactive model that made it possible to provide cash assistance ahead of anticipated drought impacts in northern Afghanistan. UN Women worked with a womens civil society organization to provide multipurpose cash assistance to 1,030 women-headed households, representing 7,599 family members. In addition, 780 women and girls received protection services, including counselling and referral support. Early-warning messages were also developed and disseminated to address information gaps identified through gender analysis and disaster-preparedness research.
Marginalized & Displaced Populations (Returnees, People with Disabilities, Climate Shocks)
Change Achieved: Restored dignity, financial agency, and self-reliance among acute risk groups.
Example (Returnees): Operated border transit centers alongside IOM at key points (Islam Qala, Torkham, Spin Boldak), assisting 96,842 returnee women and girls with protection, information, and registration services.
Example (Disabilities): Supported a central Afghanistan center providing Braille, tailoring, and small business training to women with visual or hearing impairments, enabling independent livelihood generation.
Example (Climate/Agriculture): Provided solar-powered greenhouses and water conservation assets to women in drought-affected areas, improving household nutrition and allowing women to sell surplus produce locally.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
